subject: interpreting allelic effects from fitqtl binary model

messages.author: e728ca3dc3a1a072
messages.subject: interpreting allelic effects from fitqtl binary model
parts:
I was hoping for some advice on how to interpret the allelic effect sizes ($ests) in the fitqtl ANOVA table from a stepwise model on a binary trait. I often get linked QTL, and so PVE as a measure of effect size is less satisfactory.

Given that it is a logistic regression, I assume that there is a logic link function and that the effect sizes need to be back-transformed to get the allelic effects in % (survival in my case). I also assume that some small constant is added to the 0 and 1 values because you can't take the log of 0.

Could you please give the appropriate formulate for back transforming the effect sizes from a binary model? 

I have a RIL population so I am interested in getting genotypic effect sizes (2a) if it matters.

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] interpreting allelic effects from fitqtl binary model
parts:
The estimates are derived by fitting a generalized linear model with a logit link function. No constant is added to deal with the 0's and 1's; the model is fit by maximum likelihood via iteratively reweighted least squares.

If you want genotypic effects, just multiply the estimated coefficients by 2.

I don't think you can't really back-transform the regression coefficients. We have a model like:

ln[p / (1-p)] = b0 + b1 x1 + b2 x2 + b3 x3

We can write

p / (1-p) = exp(b0) exp(b1 x1) exp(b2 x2) exp(b3 x3)

but there's no simple way to back-transform the coefficients to a linear scale, at least to my understanding.

karl
